claims.text: The CHECKPOINT-29 residual is closed: the audit now records which sim it actually ran against. Every run prints the resolved mirror path and the sha256 of sim_mirror.py. Real mirror 37ae041b..., the CHECKPOINT-29 dirty sandbox 3f1041e4... — the two runs are distinguishable from their own output alone, so a wrong-but-present mirror is now visible to any reader or replay rather than silently producing a confident verdict.

Identity is RECORDED, not asserted against a pinned expected hash. A pin would fail on every honest edit to the sim as it is developed, which would train readers to ignore the failure — the check would become noise and then be silenced. Recording makes provenance auditable without creating a brittle gate.

The first version of the verification of this fix used awk field 2, which is the colon rather than the hash, and reported 'distinguishable: NO' about output where the two hashes plainly differed. The capability worked; my check of it did not. Corrected to field 3 and the erroneous reading is recorded in the artifact rather than overwritten silently.

risks: Recording provenance makes a wrong mirror VISIBLE; it does not make it FAIL. A reader or an automated replay must actually compare the recorded hash against what they expected. If nobody reads it, this changes nothing — which is the honest limit of an observability fix.

The AB_mandatory_trajectory envelope cites a COPY of test_k03b_trajectory.py taken at promotion. That copy is now stale relative to the live file. This is correct under the frozen-hash rule — the earlier envelope documents the state at its own instant — and this envelope carries the new state with its new hash.
